Every point stays on the sphere. Anchors stay fixed. All 12 arch midpoints share the selected distance from N.

The deformation rule

Each side is a great-circle arc from N to its original equatorial anchor. Across each petal, the boundary distance is b(u) = δ + [d(u) − δ]f(u), where f(u) = u² / [w + (1 − w)u²], for −1 ≤ u ≤ 1. w is the shared M influence for all 12 petals; δ is their shared 5°–30° separation from N. This is a shape weight, not a physical force. d(u) is the spherical distance to the corresponding equatorial point.

A, B and M always refer to petal 1. The meridian panel uses C for the forward point at the selected separation; C coincides with M at azimuth 0°. This preserves the deformation used in our diagram.
